title: Finite-Sample Testing of Conditional LATE Homogeneity under Weak Compliance and Rough Assignment
banked_reason: D0.5 math PASS; BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: tier=subfield < floor=field, NOT salvageable in scope; paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < ceiling_for_field 7.4. Independent validity gate confirms downgraded bank.
gap_reasons: The delivered 8/13 and 4/5 variance-separation rates have matching same-class upper tests and fixed-sample full-record converses; the supplied proofs do not leave the advertised sharp frontier conditional on an unresolved conjecture. Conditional-CLATE homogeneity and its moment reduction already appear in [Sant’Anna’s supplement](https://psantanna.com/files/TestingTEHet-sup.pdf) and [Lu–Song, Proposition 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.12622), so novelty resides in the uniform weak-compliance separation calculation. The result covers one scalar known-uniform design and the fixed smoothness triple (1/8,1/8,1), without establishing a broader smoothness or dimensional phase diagram. The upper constant 2^50 requires n delta^3 of approximately 3 times 10^25 before the original-record power guarantee has nonempty alternatives, and the package supplies no numerical evidence establishing useful finite-sample subgroup planning. These scope and practical-calibration limits constrain the projected paper score and prevent flagship classification. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a matched finite-n, all-compliance-strength conditional-complier homogeneity frontier and repaired the pair-kernel normalization objection; the final math referee passed with no findings. The general gate assessed subfield below the field floor, with score ceiling 7.2 below 7.4 and no in-scope salvage directive, so an independent validity consultation confirmed downgraded banking. Formalization was not entered and no Lean proof or type-check is claimed; a local positioning finding remains, while a field-level re-raise requires a broader smoothness/dimension program or materially useful finite-sample calibration.
tldr: \textbf{Sharp finite-sample separation for conditional LATE homogeneity under weak compliance and rough assignment.} On the explicitly stipulated scalar-uniform H\"older benchmark, the original-record minimax variance separation is \(\rho(n,\delta)=\min\{1,(n\delta^3)^{-8/13}\}\), up to universal constants. Supplying the true propensity on the same full class changes it to \(\rho_e(n,\delta)=\min\{1,(n\delta^2)^{-4/5}\}\). Both frontiers have exact fixed-\(n\), eight-mark lower comparisons and total finite-computable attaining tests with full-null size at most \(0.10\) and power at least \(0.90\) at their certified thresholds. Exact minimization over the unknown constant uses a rank-at-most-two span without curvature inversion, grids or logarithms; unknown Lipschitz \(w\in[1,2]\) creates no additional branch. Uniform shrinking resolution requires \(n\delta_n^3\to\infty\), compared with \(n\delta_n^2\to\infty\) when propensity is supplied. Whenever original-record resolution vanishes, its profile divided by the supplied-propensity profile diverges. The clinical use is prospective subgroup-resolution planning for adjusted IV studies on this stipulated benchmark.
gap: The audited conditional-LATE testing results establish asymptotic calibration and specified local power under smoother nuisance conditions. They do not evaluate finite minimax variance separation uniformly over the prescribed shrinking-compliance experiment.
fill: The focal object is the explicit sharp separation profile with a finite attaining test, a matching full-record converse, and a necessary-and-sufficient oracle-information comparison. The supporting upper theorem derives its powers from normalized complier approximation, fine-cell adjustment-product bias and the audited Hoeffding operator envelope. The coordinate and operator noise have no additional histogram-rank factor; the trace contributes the square-root-rank quadratic noise. The same-class converse remains open.
